column19: TWO DEFECTS, multiple withdrawn. The date is wrong: the $26bn secondary was reported as planned in January 2024 and COMPLETED in early April 2024, about US$1.6bn or A$2.43bn of stock, roughly 6% of the company, against US$2.4bn of demand. And the $2,300m denominator matches no published figure at all. Canva's own number is 'more than US$2.2 billion in annualised revenue', published 24-May-2024, six weeks AFTER the sale closed. The A$3.3bn in that same sentence is the AUD translation of US$2.2bn, which is where both the phantom 2,300 and 3,300 come from.

column16: Meta Platforms
column19: RECLASSIFIED TO CONTROL. This was coded as a strategic minority investment and it is not one. Meta paid about $14.3bn for 49% of the equity; Scale then distributed the proceeds to existing shareholders and vested equity holders rather than retaining them, so mechanically primary but economically a half cash-out of the existing base, with Accel alone reported to take about $2.5bn. Founder-CEO Alexandr Wang left to run Meta's superintelligence effort with a group of employees, keeping only a board seat. A large share of the consideration is talent, not enterprise value for the data-labelling business. The $2bn denominator is a company forecast for CY2025, public 2-Apr-2025 and so at-pricing, but it is a forecast.

column16: Adobe (acquirer)
column19: CONTROL, walled off from the financing medians. Adobe agreed on 19-Nov-2025 to acquire the whole company at $12.00 a share in cash; closed 28-Apr-2026, Semrush delisted. Two label errors corrected. The $443.6m was FY2025 ACTUAL, first published 2-Mar-2026, three and a half months after pricing; the figure available at pricing was FY2025 guidance of $443.5m to $445.5m, published 6-Nov-2025. And $1,900m is EQUITY value: net cash was about $262m, so enterprise value is about $1,638m and the comparable M&A multiple is roughly 3.7x EV/FY2025E revenue, not 4.3x.
